small_guidance:
- Sweep `BLOCK_SP` in {16, 32, 64} and `BLOCK_OC` in {64, 128} with `num_warps` in {4, 8} via `triton.autotune`; with OH_POOL*OW_POOL = 196 (or similar small) and OC=128, BLOCK_SP=64/BLOCK_OC=64 may give a better dot-shape balance than 32×128.
- The inner `BLOCK_IC=64` with IC=64 means the IC loop runs once — make `BLOCK_IC` a constexpr equal to IC (drop the loop and the mask) so the compiler emits a single `tl.dot` per (kh,kw); also hoist `x_base` and reuse one `valid` mask across kh,kw boundaries that share rows/cols.
- In group_norm, switch to a single-pass Welford or load HW once into registers when CPG*HW is small (here 8*196 ≈ 1568) — make BLOCK = next_pow2(CPG*HW) and do one reduction over the whole group instead of nested static_range + re-loading for the apply pass.
large_guidance:
- Restructure the conv as an explicit im2col-GEMM where the K dimension is `IC*KH*KW` (=1600) and the M dimension is the 4 conv outputs per pooled tile flattened together (BLOCK_SP*4 rows of one matmul), so a single `tl.dot` produces all four pre-pool values and the kh/kw loop disappears — current code issues KH*KW=25 separate dots per IC tile, wasting tensor-core throughput.
- Fuse group-norm into the conv-bn-tanh-pool kernel by making one program own a full (n, group) tile: persistently accumulate the 4 pooled values for all CPG channels in registers/shared, compute mean/var across CPG*HW in-kernel, then apply affine and store — eliminates one full read+write of the pooled tensor (the dominant memory traffic now that conv is fused).
- Lay out the conv output in `channels_last` (NHWC) inside the kernel so the OC axis is the contiguous one for both the GEMM store and the subsequent group-norm reduction; this also lets the BN scale/shift broadcast happen on the fast axis.
